The absorber integrates a graphene capacitor layer and an active metasurface layer loaded with PIN diodes.
The graphene sheet resistance can be tuned from 1580 to 290 Ω/sq by varying bias voltage from −1.5 V to 3 V.
The active metasurface uses bow-tie dipole structures with PIN diodes modeled as variable resistors in series with chip inductance.
The −10 dB reflection bandwidth can be tuned from 3.55 GHz up to 19.6 GHz by adjusting bias voltages.
Reflection amplitude can be dynamically tuned between approximately −3.8 dB and −11.5 dB.
Three operation states are demonstrated: ultrawideband absorption (3.5–20 GHz), narrowband absorption (4.1–11.5 GHz), and shifted narrowband absorption (10.1–19.3 GHz).
The equivalent circuit model accurately predicts reflection performance and impedance matching.
Fabricated samples consist of 12×12 unit cells with monolayer graphene transferred onto PET and ionic liquid electrolyte sandwiched in the capacitor layer.
The metasurface substrate is Rogers5880 with ε = 2.2 and thickness 0.254 mm.
The absorber is backed by a 5.6 mm thick foam slab and a metallic ground plane.
PIN diodes used are Flip Chip MA4SPS402 from M/A-COM.
Impedance matching is controlled by tuning the resistance of the graphene layer and the diode resistance via external bias voltages.
Electric field distribution simulations show absorption dominated by metasurface resonance at some states and by graphene Salisbury absorption at others.
The absorber can switch between ultrawideband and narrowband modes by changing bias voltages applied to graphene and diodes.
The design addresses limitations of previous absorbers with narrow bandwidth and low tunability.
The absorber can dynamically adapt its electromagnetic reflection properties for potential stealth and camouflage applications.
The PIN diode resistance can be tuned from 3 Ω (on state) to 70 Ω (off state) by bias current control.
The graphene capacitor layer uses a polyethylene membrane soaked with ionic liquid electrolyte (DEME TFSI) as the dielectric.
The metasurface unit cell periodicity is 15 mm with bow-tie dipole dimensions optimized for microwave absorption.
The absorber's reflection was measured using horn antennas and a vector network analyzer in an anechoic chamber at near-normal incidence.
The absorber achieves ultrawideband absorption with an average reflection level below −10 dB over a large frequency range.
